headline: 39 MEN · 1,540 DAYS
text: Thirty-nine men held a three-kilometre island against an empire for 1,540 days — for a spice the world could get nowhere else.

headline: PULAU RUN: 3-KM OUTPOST
text: That island was Run, three kilometres long in the Banda archipelago — the world's only source of nutmeg and mace.

headline: COURTHOPE'S STAND
text: In sixteen sixteen, English captain Nathaniel Courthope arrived to break the Dutch monopoly, holding out until his death in sixteen twenty.

headline: THE ATLANTIC SETTLEMENT
text: After England seized Manhattan, the sixteen sixty-seven Treaty of Breda ended their war under uti possidetis: each side kept what it already held.

headline: THE MONOPOLY LOCK
text: England kept Manhattan; the Dutch kept Run, which completed their grip on the world's nutmeg trade.

headline: MANHATTAN VS RUN
text: Today, Manhattan is a global financial capital. And Run? A quiet island of about fifteen hundred people, where nutmeg still grows.
